title: Machine-learning analysis motivates proved criteria for Galois groups
summary: Interpretable decision trees applied to Dedekind-zeta coefficients helped the authors identify patterns in Galois extensions of degrees 4, 6, 8, 9 and 10. They formulated and proved mathematical criteria, including a nonic result: for the stated class, a₁₀₀₀(K) ≤ 4.5 implies the extension is cyclic. This theorem is a specific result; dataset classification accuracy is not a universal guarantee, and the paper reports a counterexample to an apparently perfect classifier branch. The arXiv v1 of 2025-08-08 and the 2026 journal version are one study.
ai_technology: Interpretable decision trees and logistic regression
organization: Department of Mathematics, University of Connecticut; Korea Institute for Advanced Study; Department of Mathematics, University of California, Berkeley

source_review.scope: Primary arXiv v1 and publisher full text, including result, proof scope, dates and affiliations.

evidence.tested: The authors report conventional proofs of criteria motivated by model interpretation.
evidence.unknown: The criteria apply to stated classes; model accuracy is data-dependent and a branch with apparent perfect performance has a stated out-of-sample counterexample.
evidence.ai_role: Decision-tree patterns in number-field coefficients motivated mathematical criteria that the authors then proved using conventional reasoning.
